prompt: Build TaskOutcome<T, E>, a generic type that holds either a success value or an error: implement the success/failure factories, valueOr, errorOr, and a mapValue that leaves failures untouched.
explanation: TaskOutcome has two independent type parameters, so the success channel and the error channel can be different types and the compiler still checks both. The static factories declare their own <T, E> because a static method cannot use the class's type parameters. mapValue introduces a third parameter <R> for the new value type while keeping E, which is why a failure can simply be re-wrapped as TaskOutcome<R, E> without touching the function.
hints: Both factories just call the private constructor: success passes (value, null, true) and failure passes (null, error, false).
valueOr and errorOr are one-liners built on the success flag -- return the stored field when the flag matches, otherwise the fallback.
In mapValue, handle the failure case FIRST and return TaskOutcome.failure(error) before you ever touch f.
